text.arabic_uthmani: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ بِمَكْرِهِنَّ أَرْسَلَتْ إِلَيْهِنَّ وَأَعْتَدَتْ لَهُنَّ مُتَّكَـًۭٔا وَءَاتَتْ كُلَّ وَٰحِدَةٍۢ مِّنْهُنَّ سِكِّينًۭا وَقَالَتِ ٱخْرُجْ عَلَيْهِنَّ ۖ فَلَمَّا رَأَيْنَهُۥٓ أَكْبَرْنَهُۥ وَقَطَّعْنَ أَيْدِيَهُنَّ وَقُلْنَ حَٰشَ لِلَّهِ مَا هَٰذَا بَشَرًا إِنْ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا مَلَكٌۭ كَرِيمٌۭ

words.gloss_range: sequential connector binding the scene to the prior accusation
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) makes the banquet scene answer the prior public accusation (12:30). The ayah does not open as a detached episode; it begins as a consequence, moving directly from what the women said about the wife into the counter-scene she stages.

topics.headline: sequential answer to accusation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the banquet is a counter-move to the women's public accusation in 12:30, not an isolated social scene.
topics.reason: QAC marks {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) as a connective particle, and the CRITICAL boundary row ties it specifically to the previous women's speech in 12:30.

words.gloss_range: first temporal trigger, opening the preparation panel
words.prose: {{ar:لَمَّا}} ({{tr:lammā}}) opens the first trigger: hearing produces preparation. Its payoff comes from the matching later trigger at word 24, where sight produces reaction, so the ayah is split into report-driven staging and vision-driven collapse.

topics.headline: hearing and seeing triggers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah organized by two temporal pivots: first hearing, then seeing.
topics.reason: Both {{ar:لَمَّا}} ({{tr:lammā}}) forms are marked as temporal adverbs, and the clause evidence separates the hearing clause from the later seeing clause.

words.gloss_range: she heard of/about; mediated social report becoming actionable knowledge
words.root_gloss_range: hearing, listening, and auditory reception; locally a 3fs perfect tied to mediated report through the following preposition
words.prose: {{ar:سَمِعَتْ}} ({{tr:samiʿat}}) makes the wife act from report rather than direct sight: she hears of their scheming through the following prepositional phrase. The verb also starts the first half of the ayah's perception design, where hearing sets staging in motion and later seeing overturns the women themselves. The woman discussed in 12:30 becomes the active director of the counter-scene, while the root's wider hearing register remains resonance rather than the local sense.

topics.headline: heard of the scheming
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the wife acts on mediated social report, not on something she directly witnesses.
topics.reason: QAC marks {{ar:سَمِعَتْ}} ({{tr:samiʿat}}) as 3fs perfect, and the attachment evidence governs the following {{ar:بِمَكْرِهِنَّ}} ({{tr:bi-makrihinna}}) phrase as its reported content.

topics.headline: hearing gives way to seeing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah's two panels as a sensory relay: the wife hears, then the women see.
topics.reason: The first temporal clause centers on {{ar:سَمِعَتْ}} ({{tr:samiʿat}}), while the later temporal clause centers on {{ar:رَأَيْنَهُ}} ({{tr:raʾaynahu}}).

topics.headline: public talk becomes exposure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the reversal: the woman discussed in 12:30 becomes the active director of the next scene.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows explicitly connect the hearing in 12:31 to the public speech of 12:30 and to the wife's change from object of scandal into acting subject.

topics.headline: divine hearing resonance limited
topics.reader_payoff: The reader may hear a broader root register behind the scene, while the local grammar keeps the action at the level of human report and response.
topics.reason: The root's wider Quranic profile includes divine hearing, but the local form is a 3fs human perfect with a reported-content complement, so the resonance cannot control the local sense.

words.gloss_range: their scheming; nominalized social strategy heard as the trigger of the response
words.root_gloss_range: planning, stratagem, and counter-plotting; locally a verbal noun with feminine plural possessive suffix
words.prose: {{ar:مَكْرِهِنَّ}} ({{tr:makrihinna}}) names the women's talk as strategy, not neutral conversation. As a verbal noun with their suffix, the plotting and its agents are compressed into one heard object. The word then becomes the switch that starts the wife's sending, preparing, giving, and commanding; their social strategy is answered by a staged strategy, with counter-plotting echoes such as 3:54 and 13:42 kept as resonance rather than the local sense.

topics.headline: their strategy as a heard object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the accusation has been reclassified as a concrete scheme belonging to the women.
topics.reason: QAC marks {{ar:مَكْرِهِنَّ}} ({{tr:makrihinna}}) as a verbal noun with a 3fp suffix, governed by the preceding preposition after {{ar:سَمِعَتْ}} ({{tr:samiʿat}}).

topics.headline: plot returned on its speakers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the wife answers social strategy with a staged strategy that exposes the same group.
topics.reason: The word stands before the preparation chain and locally triggers the banquet apparatus.

topics.headline: counter-plot register limited
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the larger Quranic pattern where human plotting is exposed, while the local scene remains the women's social maneuver.
topics.reason: The rows cite counter-plotting passages such as 3:54 and 13:42, but local grammar names the women's scheme as the wife's heard object rather than a direct divine action.

topics.headline: banquet apparatus begins
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this word turns prior speech into the mechanical trigger for the whole banquet setup.
topics.reason: The following verbs form a preparation sequence after the heard {{ar:مَكْرِهِنَّ}} ({{tr:makrihinna}}).

words.gloss_range: she sent or summoned toward them; directed dispatch under the wife's control
words.root_gloss_range: sending, dispatching, and message-bearing; locally Form IV 3fs human summons, not prophetic commissioning
words.prose: {{ar:أَرْسَلَتْ}} ({{tr:arsalat}}) keeps the wife as the singular controller and turns private reaction into a managed summons toward the women. The following direction to them matters: they are the target of the dispatch before they become the audience before whom Joseph is made to appear. The Quranic sending register gives the action weight, and later official sending scenes around Joseph in 12:45 and 12:50 sharpen the contrast, but the local sense remains a domestic summons.

topics.headline: wife controls the summons
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the wife converts report into a controlled summons directed at the women.
topics.reason: QAC marks {{ar:أَرْسَلَتْ}} ({{tr:arsalat}}) as Form IV 3fs perfect, and the attachment evidence ties it to the following directional phrase.

topics.headline: summons before appearance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the women first as destination of the summons and then as the audience of Joseph's staged emergence.
topics.reason: The same feminine plural group is carried by the directional phrase after {{ar:أَرْسَلَتْ}} ({{tr:arsalat}}) and by the later phrase after {{ar:اخْرُجْ}} ({{tr:ukhruj}}).

topics.headline: sending register at human scale
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a weightier Quranic sending register behind the summons, while local grammar keeps the wife as a human organizer.
topics.reason: The root often serves prophetic or official sending, but here QAC and attachment evidence identify a 3fs domestic action toward the women.

topics.headline: private and public summonses
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare the wife's private summons with later official sending around Joseph's vindication (12:45; 12:50).
topics.reason: The rows give concrete Surah 12 echoes where sending vocabulary recurs in official scenes involving Joseph (12:45; 12:50).

words.gloss_range: she prepared or made ready; deliberate arrangement of the scene
words.root_gloss_range: prepared readiness, provision, and consequence; locally a rare Form IV 3fs perfect of staged human preparation
words.prose: {{ar:أَعْتَدَتْ}} ({{tr:aʿtadat}}) presents the setting as deliberately made ready, not casually available. Its agent-beneficiary-object grammar gives the wife, the women, and the prepared object clear places in the staging, and it casts the reclining setting and knives as planned props. The rare 3fs perfect and wider preparation register heighten the planned quality, with contrastive preparation language such as 5:2 remaining resonance while the local scene stays a palace arrangement.

topics.headline: willed readiness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the banquet conditions are engineered before Joseph appears.
topics.reason: QAC marks {{ar:أَعْتَدَتْ}} ({{tr:aʿtadat}}) as Form IV 3fs perfect governing the prepared object, with the feminine plural phrase marking beneficiaries.

topics.headline: props planned before reaction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the reclining setting and knives as planned elements, not incidental scenery.
topics.reason: The preparation verb precedes both {{ar:مُتَّكَأً}} ({{tr:muttakaʾan}}) and the individualized knife distribution.

topics.headline: rare preparation register
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the unusual verbal shape sharpening the deliberateness of this one staging action.
topics.reason: The rarity and eschatological preparation register can intensify the scene, but local grammar keeps the verb as a human act of arranging a banquet setting.

topics.headline: sacred-preparation contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare the scene's manipulative readiness with wider preparation language without making that contrast the local sense.
topics.reason: The cited contrast rows supply intertextual color, including 5:2, but the local verb still denotes the wife's preparation for the women.

words.gloss_range: prepared reclining support, banquet setting, or banquet prop; locally the staged object that makes knives plausible
words.root_gloss_range: leaning, support, reclining, with debated banquet or food readings; locally a prepared accusative noun of place/object
words.prose: {{ar:مُتَّكَأً}} ({{tr:muttakaʾan}}) gives the staged scene a material setting: something prepared for reclining, support, or banquet use. Its debated pressure between support/place and food-banquet readings is useful because it explains why knives can already be in the women's hands before Joseph appears. The rare place/object form and tactile sound foreground the prop, while support and reclining echoes such as 20:18 and 76:13 sharpen the irony that bodily ease becomes bodily loss of control.

topics.headline: material banquet setting
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the setting is a concrete prepared object or place that anchors the later action.
topics.reason: QAC marks {{ar:مُتَّكَأً}} ({{tr:muttakaʾan}}) as an accusative noun of time/place serving as the object of {{ar:أَعْتَدَتْ}} ({{tr:aʿtadat}}).

topics.headline: banquet reading explains knives
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees why the knives are already plausible before the shock: the prepared setting carries banquet or food pressure.
topics.reason: The derivational and loanword debates should survive as sense pressure, but local evidence does not require replacing the support-place reading with a single food gloss.

topics.headline: comfort turns into injury
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the irony that a setting of bodily ease hosts loss of bodily control.
topics.reason: The local sequence moves from a prepared reclining or banquet object to knives, sight, and intensified cutting.

topics.headline: rare tactile form
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the unusual form and recitational texture foreground the physicality of the prop.
topics.reason: The rare noun form and variant texture support attention to the object, while they do not independently settle the lexical debate.

topics.headline: support imagery echoed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the prepared support against other leaning or reclining scenes, including 20:18 and 76:13.
topics.reason: The rows give concrete echoes for leaning or reclining imagery (20:18; 76:13), which fit the local support-place pressure.

words.gloss_range: she gave or handed; deliberate transfer to each woman
words.root_gloss_range: coming, bringing, giving, and bestowal; locally Form IV 3fs directed distribution of knives
words.prose: {{ar:آتَتْ}} ({{tr:ātat}}) keeps the wife as the single distributor while the object spreads to every woman. Its Form IV transfer makes the knives deliberately placed, not merely available. Wider provision or bestowal associations sharpen the irony, including the contrast with divine giving in 14:34; within Surah 12, later food and provision scenes in 12:37 and 12:48 make this handed blade look like an inverted provision.

topics.headline: each woman receives the instrument
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that every woman individually receives the instrument that will expose her reaction.
topics.reason: QAC marks {{ar:آتَتْ}} ({{tr:ātat}}) as Form IV 3fs, governing the distributive object phrase and culminating in the knife.

topics.headline: bestowal register inverted
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a bestowal register inverted into manipulative distribution, while the local object remains a knife.
topics.reason: The root's giving and provision range is real, but local syntax narrows the transfer to knives handed to the women.

topics.headline: given thing becomes proof
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the handed object becomes the material means by which the women reveal themselves.
topics.reason: The immediate clause gives a knife to each woman, and later local verbs show that instrument producing visible injury.

topics.headline: inverted provision scene
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare this engineered distribution with later Joseph scenes where food and provision are interpreted or managed (12:37; 12:48).
topics.reason: The row connects the giving scene with later food-arrival and provision scenes in Surah 12.

words.gloss_range: each, every; totality expressed through individual distribution
words.root_gloss_range: allness, entirety, and totality; locally accusative distributive totality in construct with the following singular
words.prose: {{ar:كُلَّ}} ({{tr:kulla}}) prevents the women from remaining an anonymous crowd. The phrase distributes the knife to each individual woman before the narrative reunites them in collective cutting and collective speech. Larger totality echoes such as 12:76 and 11:40 are secondary; the local payoff is comprehensive individual exposure.

topics.headline: each participant singled out
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that every participant personally receives a knife, so the later injury is comprehensive rather than incidental.
topics.reason: QAC marks {{ar:كُلَّ}} ({{tr:kulla}}) as the accusative distributive element before the singular feminine unit and partitive phrase.

topics.headline: individual receipt, collective reaction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the scene move from individualized responsibility to unified bodily and verbal collapse.
topics.reason: The phrase singularizes the women before later feminine plural verbs gather them back together.

topics.headline: totality echoes limited
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare local total distribution with wider totality language, while the local grammar remains about each banquet participant.
topics.reason: Rows comparing 12:76 and 11:40 provide totality resonance, but QAC fixes the local role as distributive quantifier.

words.gloss_range: one feminine individual; singular unit inside the distributive phrase
words.root_gloss_range: oneness, singularity, and unity; locally a feminine singular genitive unit after the distributive quantifier
words.prose: {{ar:وَاحِدَةٍ}} ({{tr:wāḥidatin}}) makes the distribution explicitly feminine and individual: each woman is counted as one before the single male object of sight appears. The root's later divine-oneness resonance in 12:39 is real but indirect, and the single-door warning in 12:67 adds a strategic contrast; here its first job is to divide the plural audience into accountable individuals.

topics.headline: each woman as one
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the plural group is grammatically broken into individual women before the collective reaction.
topics.reason: QAC marks {{ar:وَاحِدَةٍ}} ({{tr:wāḥidatin}}) as feminine singular genitive after {{ar:كُلَّ}} ({{tr:kulla}}), matching the implied individual woman.

topics.headline: many viewers, one seen
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the many individualized women set against the one Joseph who overwhelms them.
topics.reason: The distributive feminine singular phrase precedes masculine singular object suffixes on the later sight and magnification verbs.

topics.headline: oneness resonance limited
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear a faint contrast with Joseph's later teaching of divine oneness in 12:39, while local grammar only counts each woman.
topics.reason: The root can echo divine oneness in 12:39 and strategic singularity in 12:67, but the local form is a feminine distributive unit.

topics.headline: single-point vulnerability echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare this single gathered vulnerability with the later warning against one door in 12:67.
topics.reason: The row gives a concrete same-surah reference, 12:67, where singularity also shapes vulnerability and strategy.

words.gloss_range: a knife; concrete distributed banquet instrument that becomes a self-wounding blade
words.root_gloss_range: stillness, dwelling, tranquility, and the specialized knife noun; locally a concrete indefinite accusative instrument
words.prose: {{ar:سِكِّينًا}} ({{tr:sikkīnan}}) is the concrete thing each woman receives before Joseph appears. In the banquet setting it can begin as an ordinary cutting implement, but its placement before the reveal turns it into a prepared instrument of exposure. The lexeme is unique to this ayah, and the root's stillness and tranquility field, set against sakīna language such as 9:26, creates a sharp irony: the 'stilling' object marks the scene's most uncontrolled bodily moment.

topics.headline: knife as given object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the knife is already distributed before the visual shock occurs.
topics.reason: QAC marks {{ar:سِكِّينًا}} ({{tr:sikkīnan}}) as the accusative concrete object given to each woman.

topics.headline: dining tool becomes wound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ordinary implement become the material link between staging, shock, and wounded hands.
topics.reason: The local sequence gives a knife before the women later cut their hands, making the prop-action-body chain explicit.

topics.headline: stilling root irony
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the irony that a root associated with stillness and tranquility appears as the blade in a scene of uncontrolled motion.
topics.reason: The stillness field is etymological and distributional pressure, but the local lexical unit is the concrete knife.

topics.headline: unique knife lexeme
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this knife is a singular Quranic narrative prop attached to this scene's exposure mechanism.
topics.reason: The rows mark the lexeme as unique to this ayah, matching the unusual staged self-cutting scene.

topics.headline: tranquility contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare the knife's root with tranquility language such as 9:26 without importing that calm into the local object.
topics.reason: The rows cite tranquility passages including 9:26, but the local object remains a knife used in the hand-cutting chain.

words.gloss_range: she said; speech act introducing the command that releases Joseph into view
words.root_gloss_range: saying, speech, utterance; locally a 3fs perfect governing a quoted masculine imperative
words.prose: {{ar:قَالَتِ}} ({{tr:qālati}}) is not mere quotation packaging; it is the wife's stage direction, and the recited kasra at the junction with the following imperative tightens saying to command. After hearing, sending, preparing, and giving, her speech completes the chain by issuing the command that brings Joseph into view. The word also sets up a speech frame: her controlled command is answered by the women's uncontrolled declaration, echoing Joseph's refusal scene in 12:23 and the women's later testimony in 12:51.

topics.headline: speech executes staging
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the wife's speech is an action that completes the staging sequence.
topics.reason: QAC marks {{ar:قَالَتِ}} ({{tr:qālati}}) as 3fs perfect, and the attachment evidence makes the following imperative its speech complement.

topics.headline: recited junction tightens command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the recited junction binds 'she said' tightly to the following command.
topics.reason: The kasra before the following hamzat al-waṣl is a junction feature around {{ar:قَالَتِ}} ({{tr:qālati}}) and {{ar:اخْرُجْ}} ({{tr:ukhruj}}).

topics.headline: command answered by exclamation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees speech authority move from the wife's controlled command to the women's exposed response.
topics.reason: The ayah contains a wife-command speech verb and a later women-speech verb, framing the staging and its result.

topics.headline: speech scenes recur
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can place this command beside Joseph's refusal in 12:23 and the women's later testimony in 12:51.
topics.reason: The supplied rows explicitly connect the speech frame to concrete scenes in 12:23 and 12:51.

topics.headline: speech about God returns
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that speech invoking God in the banquet scene will recur as testimony in 12:51.
topics.reason: The rows connect the banquet speech to the later tribunal formula in 12:51.

words.gloss_range: come out; masculine singular imperative commanding Joseph into visible appearance before the women
words.root_gloss_range: going out, emerging, being brought forth, and extraction; locally a 2ms imperative of staged emergence
words.prose: {{ar:اخْرُجْ}} ({{tr:ukhruj}}) abruptly brings the absent male figure into a scene saturated with feminine plural reference. The masculine singular imperative presupposes the wife's authority over his movement, but its effect is not expulsion; it is display. With the following upon-them phrase, Joseph's entrance is staged before the women as the hinge between accusation and exposed desire, while later extraction scenes in 12:76 and 12:100 keep the root's decisive-exit register in view.

topics.headline: commanded male emergence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the shift from a female-controlled room to a masculine singular figure commanded into sight.
topics.reason: QAC marks {{ar:اخْرُجْ}} ({{tr:ukhruj}}) as a 2ms imperative, and the context supplies Joseph as the commanded addressee.

topics.headline: appearance over the audience
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees Joseph's movement as a directed appearance before the women, not a neutral entrance.
topics.reason: The attached {{ar:عَلَيْهِنَّ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhinna}}) phrase targets the women as the audience of the commanded emergence.

topics.headline: emergence exposes hidden desire
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Joseph's exit into view exposes the audience rather than simply relocating him.
topics.reason: The command is immediately answered by the women's seeing, magnifying, cutting, and speaking.

topics.headline: decisive exits in Yusuf
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare this commanded emergence with later divine extraction from prison (12:100) and another extraction scene in 12:76.
topics.reason: The cited rows give concrete kh-r-j comparisons in 12:76 and 12:100, while the local imperative remains the wife's display command.

words.gloss_range: second temporal trigger, opening the reaction panel
words.prose: {{ar:لَمَّا}} ({{tr:lammā}}) opens the second panel: once the women see him, reaction follows immediately. It answers the first {{ar:لَمَّا}} ({{tr:lammā}}) of hearing with a sharper visual trigger.

topics.headline: seeing triggers reaction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the hinge from prepared staging to immediate reaction once Joseph is seen.
topics.reason: QAC marks the second {{ar:لَمَّا}} ({{tr:lammā}}) as a temporal adverb introducing the seeing clause.

words.gloss_range: they saw him; collective female seeing of a singular male object
words.root_gloss_range: seeing, perceiving, judging, and vision; locally direct visual encounter by the women
words.prose: {{ar:رَأَيْنَهُ}} ({{tr:raʾaynahu}}) turns social judgment into direct sight. The 3fp verb with a 3ms object suffix grammatically gathers many women around one seen Joseph. Because the root can also shade into judgment or opinion, the verb answers their prior evaluation in 12:30; this direct sight also sits within Surah 12's vision pattern, from Joseph's vision in 12:4 to later dream-speech in 12:36.

topics.headline: many women see him
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the morphology of the scene: multiple female viewers encounter one masculine singular object.
topics.reason: QAC marks {{ar:رَأَيْنَهُ}} ({{tr:raʾaynahu}}) as 3fp perfect with a 3ms object suffix.

topics.headline: opinion becomes vision
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees direct sight overturn the women's earlier confident judgment about the wife.
topics.reason: The root allows seeing and assessment, and the CRITICAL rows tie this sight to the prior evaluative claim in 12:30.

topics.headline: second sensory trigger
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah's architecture: the wife hears and acts; the women see and react.
topics.reason: The seeing verb opens the second temporal panel just as hearing opened the first.

topics.headline: Yusuf sight scenes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare this direct sight with Joseph's dream vision in 12:4 and later dream-speech in 12:36.
topics.reason: The rows give concrete sight-related references in 12:4 and 12:36, while local sense remains physical seeing.

topics.headline: same object through response
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices Joseph remains the single grammatical focus from sight into overwhelming estimation.
topics.reason: The same 3ms suffix appears on {{ar:رَأَيْنَهُ}} ({{tr:raʾaynahu}}) and {{ar:أَكْبَرْنَهُ}} ({{tr:akbarnahu}}).

words.gloss_range: they magnified him, found him great, or were overwhelmed by him; local reaction before bodily loss of control
words.root_gloss_range: greatness, magnitude, age, seniority, and overwhelming estimation; locally Form IV feminine plural reaction to Joseph
words.prose: {{ar:أَكْبَرْنَهُ}} ({{tr:akbarnahu}}) turns sight into overwhelming estimation. Its feminine plural form with the same masculine singular suffix keeps all women responding to one Joseph, and its Form IV shape emphasizes their caused reaction rather than Joseph's objective greatness alone. The verb then presses directly into the hand-cutting, so mental awe, possible bodily disruption, and loss of motor control are staged in sequence; later k-b-r scenes of age and senior weight in 12:78 and 12:80 remain echo rather than local sense.

topics.headline: they hold him great
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the women collectively magnify one male object, keeping Joseph as the grammatical center.
topics.reason: QAC marks {{ar:أَكْبَرْنَهُ}} ({{tr:akbarnahu}}) as Form IV 3fp with a 3ms object suffix.

topics.headline: awe becomes bodily loss
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the sequence move from perception to overwhelming estimation to physical loss of control.
topics.reason: The verb stands immediately between seeing and intensified cutting in the local sequence.

topics.headline: bodily-disruption reading limited
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that classical discussion can make the overwhelm bodily, while the local minimum remains awe that leads into cutting.
topics.reason: The physiological reading is attested as lexical discussion, but the local narrative explicitly supplies the following bodily effect through {{ar:قَطَّعْنَ}} ({{tr:qaṭṭaʿna}}).

topics.headline: greatness drives classification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees how their magnification prepares the later denial of human category and assertion of angelic category.
topics.reason: The verb precedes the final speech in which the women deny Joseph is human and call him a noble angel.

topics.headline: greatness echoes later weight
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare this overwhelmed greatness with later age and seniority uses in 12:78 and 12:80.
topics.reason: The rows cite concrete later Surah 12 references where k-b-r marks age, seniority, or weight (12:78; 12:80).

topics.headline: subjective estimation form
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the form highlights the women's reaction rather than only a static quality in Joseph.
topics.reason: Form IV supports an estimation or caused-response reading in this context.

words.gloss_range: they cut repeatedly or intensely; active feminine plural self-injury under involuntary shock
words.root_gloss_range: cutting, severing, fragmentation, and rupture; locally Form II intensified cutting of possessed hands
words.prose: {{ar:قَطَّعْنَ}} ({{tr:qaṭṭaʿna}}) is where visual overwhelm becomes physical evidence. The grammar is active and feminine plural, but the sequence makes the action narratively involuntary: they see, are overwhelmed, and cut their own hands. Form II and its doubled sound intensify the cutting, while the later recall in 12:50 makes the wound judicial evidence; severe hand-cutting language such as 5:38 remains contrast, not the local legal sense.

topics.headline: active grammar, involuntary scene

topics.reason: QAC marks {{ar:أَيْدِيَهُنَّ}} ({{tr:aydiyahunna}}) as a plural concrete noun with a 3fp possessive suffix.

topics.headline: hands act and suffer

Structurally, the ayah moves from each woman's individual test to their collective shaped utterance, and the women who spoke accusation in 12:30 now speak amazement in 12:31 before their formal testimony in 12:51.

topics.headline: voice after wound

topics.headline: each becomes one voice

words.gloss_range: exculpatory or distancing exclamation; frozen formula opening their speech
words.root_gloss_range: distancing, exclusion, or exculpatory recoil; locally an uninflected exclamatory formula before the God-name
words.prose: {{ar:حَاشَ}} ({{tr:ḥāsha}}) opens the women's speech with formulaic recoil before the human/angel classification and turns shock Godward through the following formula. Its uninflected shape and variant-sensitive endings make the utterance feel frozen and exclamatory, not a normal finite verb. The same formula returns when the women testify for Joseph in 12:51, so beauty's shock and innocence's proof are linked by the two rare Surah 12 occurrences.

topics.headline: formulaic recoil
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speech begins with a fixed exculpatory formula before any classification is stated.
topics.reason: QAC marks {{ar:حَاشَ}} ({{tr:ḥāsha}}) as an uninflected verbal or exclamatory form.

topics.headline: exclamation directed to God
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the exclamation turns shock Godward before the women deny ordinary humanity.
topics.reason: The following {{ar:لِلَّهِ}} ({{tr:li-llāhi}}) completes the exclamatory formula before the negation clauses.

topics.headline: beauty and innocence formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the same rare formula link the banquet reaction with the women's later testimony in 12:51.

words.gloss_range: God's name in the exculpatory formula; theological opening to the classification
words.root_gloss_range: God-name and worship/awe associations; locally genitive proper name governed by the preceding preposition in the formula

The name will recur in the same formula at 12:51, moving from stunned beauty to public innocence, and it can be compared with Joseph's deliberate monotheistic teaching in 12:39 and another crisis invocation in 12:90. Root discussions about bewilderment and worship are best kept as resonance; the local word is the divine proper name in a fixed formula.

topics.headline: classification under God-invocation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the denial of humanity and assertion of angelic nobility begin from God-invocation.
topics.reason: QAC marks {{ar:اللَّهِ}} ({{tr:allāhi}}) as the genitive proper name governed by the preceding preposition in the formula.

topics.headline: beauty formula becomes testimony
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the God-name carry the scene from involuntary astonishment to later public testimony in 12:51.
topics.reason: The rows explicitly tie the formula in 12:31 to its repetition at 12:51.

topics.headline: bewilderment and worship resonance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader may feel the invocation as awe-filled bewilderment, while local grammar keeps the word as God's proper name.
topics.reason: Root associations around bewilderment and worship can color the reaction, but they do not replace the divine-name function in {{ar:حَاشَ لِلَّهِ}} ({{tr:ḥāsha li-llāhi}}).

topics.headline: God-name anticipates teaching
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare the women's involuntary God-invocation with Joseph's deliberate monotheistic teaching in 12:39.

topics.headline: God-name at crisis points

topics.reason: The row supplies the concrete same-surah references 12:31, 12:51, and 12:90.

words.gloss_range: a human being, embodied mortal; accusative predicate under negation
words.root_gloss_range: human embodied being, skin, and good-news branches; locally the negated human category in the first classification clause
words.prose: {{ar:بَشَرًا}} ({{tr:basharan}}) is the category the women deny. Its accusative shape belongs to the governing negation construction, while variant case patterns can change the grammar without changing the denial. The embodied-human pressure matters because the next clause replaces that category with an angelic one; this inverts passages such as 11:27 where people reduce a messenger to ordinary humanity, and later good-news use in 12:96 remains root resonance rather than the local meaning.

topics.headline: negated human predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the grammar formally marks the denied category as the predicate under negation.
topics.reason: QAC marks {{ar:بَشَرًا}} ({{tr:basharan}}) as accusative predicate in the negated copular construction.

topics.headline: case contrast preserves denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that variant case patterns change grammatical analysis while preserving the denial of humanness.
topics.reason: The qiraat rows expose governing and non-governing negation patterns but do not overturn the local canonical accusative.

topics.headline: embodied humanity denied
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the women deny ordinary embodied humanity, not merely social status.
topics.reason: The local clause opposes {{ar:بَشَرًا}} ({{tr:basharan}}) to {{ar:مَلَكٌ}} ({{tr:malakun}}), making human versus angel the explicit semantic contrast.

topics.headline: messenger polemic inverted
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare this scene with passages where people deny messengers by insisting they are merely human, such as 11:27.
topics.reason: The cited rows give concrete human/messenger and human/angel contrasts, including 11:27, 6:91, 17:93, and 21:3.

topics.headline: good-news branch is later resonance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can trace the b-sh-r root from denied humanity here to good news near restoration in 12:96, while the local word still means human being.
topics.reason: The good-news branch appears in the later cited root use, but local syntax and opposition to angel select the human-being branch.

topics.headline: denial answered by angel
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the negated human category is immediately answered by the asserted noble angel category.
topics.reason: The final clause supplies the positive classification after the negated predicate.

words.gloss_range: negative particle in a restriction frame
words.prose: {{ar:إِنْ}} ({{tr:in}}) is negative here, not conditional. It opens the restrictive frame completed by the later exceptive particle, so the women's second classification is not a comparison but an exclusive claim.

topics.headline: not conditional, restrictive
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final clause restricts the possible classification to one claim.
topics.reason: QAC identifies {{ar:إِنْ}} ({{tr:in}}) as a negation particle in the {{ar:إِنْ}} ({{tr:in}})-{{ar:إِلَّا}} ({{tr:illā}}) frame.

words.gloss_range: exceptive particle completing the exclusive classification
words.prose: {{ar:إِلَّا}} ({{tr:illā}}) completes the restriction opened by the preceding negative particle. It funnels the women's final verdict into the compact noble-angel predicate, making the closing category exclusive rather than merely heightened praise.

topics.headline: only a noble angel
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah's final classification is exclusive, not comparative.
topics.reason: QAC marks {{ar:إِلَّا}} ({{tr:illā}}) as the exceptive particle completing the negative-restrictive construction.

words.gloss_range: an angel; indefinite nominative predicate in the exclusive classification
words.root_gloss_range: angelic being, kingship/authority by vowel distinction, and possession/sovereignty; locally the angel category, not the king reading
words.prose: {{ar:مَلَكٌ}} ({{tr:malakun}}) supplies the positive category after humanity has been denied. Its indefinite nominative shape classifies Joseph as an angelic type, not as a named angel, lifting him into an exalted nonhuman category. Variant and root proximity to kingship are meaningful in this royal surah, especially beside royal m-l-k scenes in 12:43, 12:50, and 12:54, but the canonical local reading remains angel; the claim also reverses prophetic denials of angelic status such as 11:31.

topics.headline: angel as category
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the women classify Joseph as an angelic type, not as a specific named angel.
topics.reason: QAC marks {{ar:مَلَكٌ}} ({{tr:malakun}}) as nominative indefinite predicate after the restriction frame.

topics.headline: human replaced by angel

topics.reason: The local human-denial clause is answered by {{ar:إِنْ هَذَا إِلَّا مَلَكٌ}} ({{tr:in hādhā illā malakun}}).

topics.headline: angel versus king proximity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a short-vowel shift can move the word toward kingship, while the canonical local predicate is angel.
topics.reason: Variant rows are valid contrast evidence, but the local canonical surface and following adjective support the angel reading.

topics.headline: angelic and royal domains
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the m-l-k root resonate with Joseph's later royal setting in 12:43, 12:50, and 12:54 while retaining the immediate angelic sense.
topics.reason: The rows supply concrete royal-domain references in Surah 12 where m-l-k appears in kingly contexts.

words.gloss_range: noble, honored, excellent; adjective completing the final angel predicate
words.root_gloss_range: nobility, generosity, honor, and elevated worth; locally an indefinite nominative adjective modifying the angel predicate
words.prose: {{ar:كَرِيمٌ}} ({{tr:karīmun}}) is the ayah's landing word, completing the compact noble-angel predicate with a paired indefinite cadence. It does not merely intensify 'angel'; it specifies an honored and noble kind of being, borrowing an elevated honor register also heard in sacred uses such as 56:77. The same root frames Joseph earlier when his lodging is to be honored in 12:21, so the banquet verdict returns household honor as public, involuntary recognition.

topics.headline: noble modifies angel
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final word grammatically completes the two-word angel predicate.
topics.reason: QAC marks {{ar:كَرِيمٌ}} ({{tr:karīmun}}) as an indefinite nominative masculine adjective agreeing with {{ar:مَلَكٌ}} ({{tr:malakun}}).

topics.headline: honored noble being

topics.reason: The root range includes nobility, honor, and generosity, and the local adjective qualifies the angel predicate.

topics.headline: closing word of exalted classification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ayah close on a compact, paired formula of angelic nobility.
topics.reason: The word stands at ayah closure, and the paired indefinite cadence of the final two words supports the compact classification.

topics.headline: honor returns publicly

topics.reason: The rows give 12:21 as the concrete earlier k-r-m frame around Joseph in the household.

topics.headline: sacred honor register limited

topics.reason: The adjective appears in sacred and honorific registers elsewhere, including 56:77, but the local referent is Joseph in the women's speech.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The chain from hearing their talk through sending, preparing, equipping each woman, commanding an emergence, seeing, cutting, and collective speech.
baseline_models.mechanism: A controlled host converts circulating talk into repeatable embodied witness. Uniform provisioning and a timed reveal move every spectator from report to sight, involuntary act, and a shared verdict.

activation_trace.role: The public-circulation branch casts the inciting hearing as reputation moving through a group.
The dispatch branch supplies the deliberate gathering of the future witnesses.
The ready-at-hand branch makes the setting prearranged rather than improvised.
The totalizing branch extends the experimental condition across the whole audience.
The numerical-one branch makes every spectator an individually equipped witness.
The knife branch supplies the common instrument that will register the reaction bodily.
The spoken-word branch brackets the test with her command and their resulting declaration.
The disclosure branch makes his entrance a timed uncovering of what the room has not yet seen.
The ocular-perception branch is the switch that converts the arranged conditions into bodily evidence.
The severing branch records an involuntary material outcome that mere polite speech cannot counterfeit.

changed_reading.before: A hostess invites critics to a meal, shows them Joseph, and they react dramatically to his beauty.
changed_reading.after: The meal is an engineered witness procedure: rumor is forced through identical conditions into sight, wounds, and a collective utterance.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The supported setting, the knives held by the women, their magnification of the seen figure, and the cutting of their own hands.
baseline_models.mechanism: The scene begins with bodily support and possession of a tool, then vision enlarges its object while fragmenting the spectators' bodily control. The wounds remain literal, while the hand branches also expose a collapse of power and action.

activation_trace.role: The leaning-and-support branch establishes composed, supported bodies before their loss of composure.
The slaughter-stilling branch gives the utensil an inherent capacity to terminate controlled motion.
The inward-magnification branch locates the perceptual excess in the viewers' own estimation.
The division branch turns a single visual shock into fragmentation enacted on their bodies.
The bodily-hand branch preserves the direct reading of actual self-inflicted wounds.
The non-dominant strength branch permits a simultaneous reading in which their practical power fails.
The cohesion branch supplies a secondary contrast between the figure they name and the viewers who come apart in action.

changed_reading.before: The women are startled and accidentally cut their physical hands.
changed_reading.after: The literal wounds remain primary, but they also display a transfer of agency: as the viewers magnify him, their own capacity to hold, distinguish, and govern action fragments.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: After direct sight, the women negate the category of human being and replace it with an angelic and noble category.
baseline_models.mechanism: Negation followed by exception records a failed classification. The visible human surface exceeds the spectators' available human category, so their speech relocates the seen figure into angelic nobility rather than merely adding a compliment.

activation_trace.role: The direct-sight branch makes the categorical utterance an effect of encounter rather than report.
The defining-word branch makes their speech draw a boundary around what kind of being can be before them.
The visible-surface branch grounds the denial in the very exterior that sight has encountered.
The human-being branch supplies the category explicitly rejected by the spectators.
The angel branch supplies the replacement category asserted after the human one fails.
The honor branch qualifies the replacement category with intrinsic dignity rather than mere strangeness.

changed_reading.before: The women use ornamental hyperbole to praise exceptional human beauty.
changed_reading.after: Their words enact a sight-induced category failure: human surface is denied and replaced by an honored angelic class, while the claim remains the spectators' shocked reading rather than narrator-level disambiguation.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier instrumented extraction classifies Joseph as a boy, conceals him as merchandise, and moves him through a deficient price toward honored lodging. The focus stages a second controlled emergence whose witnesses revoke ordinary humanity and publicly name angelic nobility. The second reveal therefore reverses the social valuation produced by the first.

activation_trace.role: The bucket branch supplies the first instrumented extraction of the hidden figure.
The concealment branch shows that the first discovery is immediately returned to social hiding.
The tradable-piece branch converts the discovered person into merchandise.
The exchange branch places that human classification inside a market transaction.
The price branch supplies the scale on which his earlier public value is measured.
The diminution branch marks that market valuation as an active reduction of worth.
The lodging-and-guest branch moves the valued object into a protected domestic place.
The honor branch begins a private revaluation that the focus later makes public.
The focus disclosure branch reprises extraction as a commanded visual unveiling.
The human category is the valuation explicitly withdrawn in the second reveal.
The angel category replaces the earlier boy-and-merchandise classification.
The final honor branch completes the movement from deficient price to declared nobility.

structural_cues: 12:19 announces a boy and then conceals him as merchandise; 12:31 answers the reveal with a denial of ordinary humanity.
The sequence runs from deficient price, through a charge to honor his lodging, to collective public naming as noble.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two mediated appearances and a sequence of opposed valuations. I infer that the focus deliberately reprises discovery in order to reverse objectification; a live alternative is that the parallel only escalates other people's reactions without undoing the earlier market status.

changed_reading.before: The focus is a self-contained demonstration of exceptional beauty.
changed_reading.after: It is also a counter-discovery and public repricing: the figure once extracted, hidden, and cheaply commodified is brought out again and declared beyond the category that enabled that reduction.

context_deltas.mechanism: The private encounter closes entrances, then Joseph's sight of a proof participates in diversion and escape from harm. The focus reverses the spatial and causal sequence: he is commanded outward, the women see him, and their action is diverted into their own hands. Vision is thus a directional test of self-command rather than a neutral intake of beauty.

activation_trace.role: The secured-closure branch establishes the earlier encounter as a sealed private scene.
The entrance branch supplies the threshold whose closing and reopening organize the contrast.
The earlier direct-sight branch initiates a perceptual chain that protects the seer from acting.
The proof branch gives the earlier sight an orienting object rather than a merely attractive one.
The turning-away branch supplies the protective directional result of that earlier sight.
The escape-from-entanglement branch marks the preserved alternative to captured desire.
The outward-motion branch reopens the scene and places Joseph before multiple viewers.
The repeated sight branch lets the focus invert the earlier seeing-to-restraint sequence.
The severing branch is the harmful action into which the spectators' attention is redirected.
The bodily-hand branch localizes the reversed consequence in the viewers themselves.

structural_cues: 12:23-24 moves from closed doors through seeing a proof to the diversion of harm.
12:31 moves from commanded emergence through seeing Joseph to self-directed bodily harm.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two sight-centered causal chains with opposed outcomes. I infer that their juxtaposition tests what vision does to agency; a live alternative is that the repeated seeing vocabulary is plot continuity without a designed ethical contrast.

changed_reading.before: The women's sight is simply an overwhelming aesthetic perception.
changed_reading.after: Their sight is the inverse of Joseph's earlier seeing: one perception redirects threatened action away from harm, while the other redirects action into the seers' own bodies.

context_deltas.mechanism: Before the focus, a cut garment becomes a directional sign that adjudicates incompatible speech. In the focus, distributed cuts on hands accompany a unanimous utterance. The earlier forensic pattern changes the wounds from mere symptoms into material witnesses that verify the force of the encounter and expose the spectators' prior judgment.

activation_trace.role: The lengthwise-cut branch supplies the first wound-like trace whose form carries information.
The garment branch provides the material surface on which the earlier event leaves evidence.
The back-side branch makes orientation, not speech alone, decide the earlier dispute.
The evidentiary-mark branch authorizes a material trace to function as a witness.
The truthful-speech branch supplies one verdict that the earlier cut is asked to establish.
The false-speech branch supplies the opposed verdict sorted by the physical evidence.
The focus severing branch repeats the production of a bodily legible trace.
The deeds-attributed-to-hands branch lets the wounds attest to their owners' involuntary action.
The speech branch places the women's declaration beside the wounds that corroborate it.

structural_cues: 12:25-27 asks a cut surface to distinguish truth from falsehood.
12:31 couples cuts on each witness with a shared spoken classification.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a nearby forensic cut and then a room of self-cutting speakers. I infer that the first pattern licenses the second cuts as testimony; a live alternative is that only the shirt is juridical evidence and the hand wounds remain affective symptoms.

changed_reading.before: The wounds merely measure the intensity of the women's surprise.
changed_reading.after: The wounds also testify: like the earlier cut garment, they make a contested account materially legible and turn the judges into evidence.

context_deltas.mechanism: An attempted turning-away and covering is followed by city-wide women's talk that claims to see the woman in evident error. The focus begins when she hears that circulation and answers by making the remote judges actually see. Their propositional judgment is converted into first-person bodily evidence, allowing her to seize the medium of judgment.

activation_trace.role: The turning-aside branch supplies the failed attempt to remove the affair from public attention.
The protective-covering branch supplies the concealment that public speech subsequently defeats.
The women-as-group branch identifies a social judging body rather than an isolated critic.
The gathered-city branch expands their speech into an urban reputation network.
The considered-opinion branch marks their first seeing as a judgment about another person's state.
The deviation branch supplies the adverse category imposed by the remote judges.
The manifestness branch gives their remote judgment its claim of obviousness.
The reputation branch carries that city judgment into the woman's hearing.
The direct-sight branch replaces their distant opinion with immediate encounter.
The circulating-saying branch shows her staged answer generating a new collective formulation.

structural_cues: The command to turn away and cover the affair is followed immediately by talk among women in the city.
The women first say that they see her condition; in the focus, the same root shifts to their direct sight of him.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an attempted cover, reputational circulation, and a shift from evaluative seeing to ocular seeing. I infer that the hostess designs an epistemic trap to convert hearsay into firsthand evidence; a live alternative is that the two uses of seeing are ordinary senses without a deliberate media reversal.

changed_reading.before: She seeks sympathy by showing the women what attracted her.
changed_reading.after: She takes control of how knowledge is produced: distant judges who claimed clear vision are compelled into direct sight, and their bodies replace rumor with firsthand testimony.

context_deltas.mechanism: The women diagnose love as having reached an inward heart boundary and call the condition manifest error. The focus redistributes that hidden bodily penetration onto the diagnosticians as visible cuts in their hands. Their own surfaces now bear an external analogue of the inward wound they had attributed to her.

activation_trace.role: The heart-penetration branch supplies the hidden bodily depth of the woman's passion.
The heart-core branch locates the diagnosed attachment at an interior center.
The manifestness branch creates tension between their claim of obvious diagnosis and its still-hidden bodily locus.
The encompassing branch distributes the counter-demonstration across the judging group.
The severing branch gives the judges a wound of their own.
The bodily-hand branch places the new wounds on an exposed and publicly inspectable surface.
The visible-surface branch sharpens the movement from an inwardly named passion to outward bodily evidence.

structural_cues: 12:30 locates her love at the heart's inner covering while the women judge it from outside.
12:31 gives those judges visible wounds after their own encounter with the same object of desire.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an inward heart image followed by outward hand wounds. I supply the metaphorical transfer from her hidden penetration to their visible cuts; a live alternative is simple shared attraction with no wound-for-wound correspondence.

changed_reading.before: The women finally experience an attraction comparable to hers.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the demonstration transfers her inwardly diagnosed wound onto their visible bodies, making the judges carry an external version of what they mocked.

context_deltas.mechanism: Surrounding verses name feminine maneuvering as powerful artifice. In the focus, the woman answers the women's talk with ordered dispatch, preparation, individual equipment, and a command. She then uses their reaction against their blame, restates solicitation, and threatens confinement and humiliation; Joseph subsequently speaks of plural feminine invitation. The demonstration can therefore be read as forming a coercive social field, not only winning an argument.

activation_trace.role: The artifice branch supplies an explicit local name for strategic feminine action before the focus.
The magnitude-and-power branch marks that strategy as consequential rather than trivial.
The successive-group branch frames her invitation as the assembly of a social body.
The prepositioned-readiness branch makes the encounter operationally prepared.
The encompassing branch places every attendee inside the same arranged pressure.
The one-by-one branch shows the field being built through separately equipped participants.
The effective-speaker branch gives her command an organizing force within the room.
The commanded exit is the timed act around which the assembled audience is synchronized.
The blame branch shows her immediately converting their reaction into a rebuttal of their criticism.
The solicitation branch reveals that the demonstration has not ended the underlying pressure on Joseph.
The preserving-restraint branch identifies the resistance that the social field seeks to overcome.
The binding-command branch turns attraction into an explicit demand.
The confinement branch supplies the threatened consequence of resisting the demand.
The humiliation branch adds social degradation to physical confinement.
The plural calling-and-inclining branch extends the pressure beyond a single speaker.
The repeated artifice branch names the collective pressure from Joseph's side of the encounter.
The heart-inclining branch states the susceptibility that makes the pressure dangerous.

structural_cues: 12:28 labels feminine strategy as powerful; the focus answers women's talk with a tightly ordered sequence of assembly and display.
12:32 moves directly from using the spectators' reaction against their blame to solicitation, command, prison, and humiliation.
12:33 speaks of plural feminine invitation and artifice rather than only the first woman's private desire.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the strategic labels, the arranged display, the immediate threat, and later plural pressure. I infer that the focus recruits or at least mobilizes the audience into a coercive field; a live alternative is that the women remain witnesses and the later plural does not result from this assembly.

changed_reading.before: The woman stages the scene to vindicate her attraction before her critics.
changed_reading.after: Vindication remains, but the display also builds leverage around Joseph: individually prepared spectators become a synchronized social field in which solicitation can be backed by command, shame, and confinement.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus opens with a human hearing that understands circulating speech and answers it by constructing a spectacle. After Joseph voices danger, divine hearing is paired with an answered plea, disclosed knowledge, and the diversion of the women's artifice. Two hearing-to-action loops oppose one another: one intensifies exposure, the other protects from its coercive aftermath.

activation_trace.role: The understanding-and-response branch makes the woman's hearing the causal start of her intervention.
The answering-speech branch supplies the protective response to Joseph's preceding plea.
The diversion branch gives the second hearing loop an outcome opposite to the woman's staged intensification.
The artifice branch identifies the danger that the answering action turns away.
The repeated responsive-hearing branch closes the causal echo begun by the focus.
The disclosed-knowledge branch distinguishes protective comprehension from mere reception of sound.

structural_cues: 12:31 begins with hearing followed by a deliberate human response.
12:33-34 moves from Joseph's spoken plea to answered diversion and closes by naming hearing and knowledge.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two hearing-triggered responses with opposite effects. I infer a causal echo in which responsive divine hearing counters responsive human hearing; a live alternative is that the repeated root only links ordinary hearing with a closing divine attribute.

changed_reading.before: The opening hearing only explains why the woman invites the critics.
changed_reading.after: Her hearing initiates one intervention in a contest over speech, while the later responsive hearing initiates a counter-intervention that diverts the danger her spectacle helped consolidate.

context_deltas.mechanism: Joseph's commanded exit occurs between secured domestic doors and a later decision to confine him despite visible signs. The focus is therefore an aperture in a custody sequence: he is exposed when another actor needs his visibility, then contained again after that visibility produces socially dangerous knowledge.

activation_trace.role: The firm-closure branch supplies the domestic enclosure preceding the focus.
The entrance branch identifies the controlled threshold through which access is managed.
The outward-motion branch marks a temporary opening rather than autonomous departure.
The disclosure branch shows that his visibility is activated for someone else's purpose.
The direct-sight branch supplies the knowledge generated during the temporary exposure.
The appearing branch marks the later decision as arising after matters have become visible.
The after-before branch makes confinement follow, rather than precede, recognized evidence.
The visible-sign branch confirms that renewed containment does not result from lack of evidence.
The confinement branch closes the aperture opened by the focus.
The appointed-time branch turns recontainment into an administratively sustained condition.

structural_cues: The private episode secures the doors; the focus orders Joseph outward before a selected audience.
After signs have been seen, the later response is prison until a time rather than release or public vindication.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies closure, commanded appearance, recognized signs, and subsequent confinement. I infer a managed-exposure cycle in which visibility is granted and withdrawn by others; a live alternative is that the focus exit is ordinary room movement and prison follows for unrelated political reasons.

changed_reading.before: The command to come out is a simple entrance into the banquet scene.
changed_reading.after: It is a controlled aperture between enclosures: Joseph is made visible for a social purpose, and the resulting recognition does not free him but helps make renewed containment expedient.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates a form-distant agricultural branch rather than the ordinary sense of the focus noun. It remains anchored in that noun, the explicit preparation, the prior seed branch, and the produced cuts; downstream prose must present it only as a material analogy for cultivated reaction, never as a replacement lexical gloss.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The woman hears the women's makr, prepares the conditions, and obtains a distributed bodily and verbal yield.

activation_trace.role: The irrigation branch frames hostile talk as moisture that makes hard social ground workable.
The readiness branch supplies the deliberate cultivation of conditions before the reveal.
The seed branch gives the preceding love-talk latent material that can be made to grow visibly.
The division branch supplies the distributed bodily yield of the prepared encounter.

changed_reading.before: She answers hostile talk with a clever demonstration.
changed_reading.after: As a contained material analogy, the hostile talk irrigates the very ground she then prepares, allowing latent desire to emerge as a harvest of divided hands and changed speech.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates a branch of the support-setting root that concerns restraint of the mouth. It remains anchored in the movement from heard public speech to a prepared setting and replacement speech; downstream prose must mark it as wordplay-like imagistic pressure, not claim that the furniture literally means silencing.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus moves from circulating talk, through a prepared muttaka, to the same speakers replacing blame with an exclamation.

activation_trace.role: The reputation branch supplies the mouths whose circulating speech provokes the scene.
The mouth-restraining branch figures the prepared support as a device for stopping the prior discourse.
The circulating-saying branch shows that silencing occurs by replacement with a new shared utterance.

changed_reading.before: The prepared support is only part of the hospitality setting.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, it also images a mouth-closing operation: she does not rebut the rumor but makes its speakers replace it with their own astonished verdict.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it reads tribute, hand-to-hand exchange, and reward-seeking gift branches across an ordinary act of giving utensils. It remains anchored in giving each woman a knife and receiving wounded hands plus honorific speech; downstream prose must qualify it as a transactional analogy, not a literal sale or tribute.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The woman gives each attendee a knife and receives from the equipped group both bodily marks and a public declaration of nobility.

activation_trace.role: The earlier price branch supplies the valuation economy that this later exchange reverses.
The tribute branch makes the provisioning legible as an advance that solicits a return.
The hand-to-hand branch turns the wounded hands into the bodily medium of return.
The gift-seeking-recompense branch lets their declaration of nobility function as the requested social return.
The spoken-word branch supplies the public payment produced by the arranged giving.

changed_reading.before: She provides table utensils and receives an unplanned reaction.
changed_reading.after: As a contained exchange analogy, the knives are advanced and the women repay the hostess with wounded hands and a noble classification, furnishing a counter-price to Joseph's earlier undervaluation.

strongest_changes: The banquet becomes an engineered witness procedure that converts circulating judgment into direct sight, bodily evidence, and changed speech.
The nearby forensic shirt makes the women's cuts readable as testimony, not only as symptoms of astonishment.
The focus reprises Joseph's first extraction but reverses boy, merchandise, and deficient price into denied humanity, angelic classification, and public nobility.
The commanded emergence is temporary managed exposure between domestic closure and later prison despite recognized signs.
The spectators' reaction can serve both self-vindication and the construction of a coercive social field around Joseph.
summary.what_was_special: The focus concentrates rumor, controlled hospitality, visual encounter, bodily fracture, and taxonomic speech into one causal apparatus. Context repeatedly changes that apparatus: discovery becomes revaluation, vision splits into restraint or loss of control, cuts become witnesses, inward passion becomes outward wound, and disclosure remains compatible with coercion and recontainment.
remaining_uncertainties: The hand-as-lost-power reading coexists with the direct bodily wound and should not displace it.
The women's plural invitation after the focus may indicate mobilization by the spectacle, but the packet does not force that causal antecedent.
The human-to-angel classification belongs to shocked speakers and need not be promoted to narrator-level ontology.
The cultivation, mouth-closing, and exchange outliers depend on branch-distant material analogies and require explicit qualification.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Public circulation is answered by a controlled demonstration.** س م ع B005 (reputation and public circulation), ع ت د B001 (prepared and present), and خ ر ج B001 (passing out from within) form a staged sequence. I infer that she counters reported speech by arranging direct sight under conditions she controls. The banquet reads as an evidentiary performance, not merely hospitality.
2. **Visual magnification interrupts bodily control.** ر ء ي B001, ك ب ر B003 (regarding something as great), ق ط ع B001 (severing), and ي د ي B001 (bodily hand) supply perception, valuation, and injury. I infer that absorbed perception suspends ordinary sensorimotor attention. Their cut hands become involuntary testimony to the force of what they saw.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 12:50 recalled the cut hands as durable evidence, and 12:51 turned the staged spectators into exonerating witnesses.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Physical severing as loss of practical continuity.** `ق ط ع:B001` is physical cutting or repeated scratching; `ق ط ع:B002` is a separated piece or portion. The sequence carefully assigns seating, food-setting, a knife to each woman, a visual entrance, magnification, then cut hands; 12:32 uses their reaction to justify prior solicitation. Those elements are supplied; I infer that astonishment interrupts the ordinary hand-tool relation and externalizes divided attention. *Qaṭṭaʿna aydiyahunna* reads as bodily evidence of a perception strong enough to sever coordinated action.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 12:50 explicitly reopens the question of the women who cut their hands, so the bodily interruption that first exposed astonishment becomes durable evidence in Joseph's delayed case review.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak sözü işitmeyi yalnızca ses almak olarak değil, sözü anlamak ve ardından kabul edip uymak olarak açıklar. Dalın anlama ve yerine getirme çerçevesi bu katmanlı anlamı doğru yansıtır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın biçimin anlam ve davranış sonucuna uzanan kullanımını verir; yalnız belirli bir söz öbeğine bağlı ek kapsam yüklemez.

concept_map.definition: İşitilen sözü anlamak ve bağlama göre onu kabul ederek gereğini yerine getirmektir.

facets.statement: İşitilen sözün anlamı kavranır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar işitmeyi bilişsel ve davranışsal bir sonuçla açıklar: söz anlaşılır, ardından kabul veya uyma gerçekleşebilir.

concept_gloss.applicability: İşitilen sözün kavranmasından kabulüne ve gereğinin yapılmasına kadar uzanan çekirdeği birlikte karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Anlama, kabul ve davranışa geçirme aşamalarını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Birinin söylediğini anlayıp kabul etme veya öğüdüne uyma bağlamında doğal bir karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Sözü kavrama, kabul etme ve ona uyma yönlerini bağlam içinde korur.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: sözü anlayıp kabul etmek ve ona uymak

error_profile.preserves: Sözün kişi tarafından işitilmiş olmasını korur.
error_profile.loses: Anlama, kabul etme ve gereğini yerine getirme sonuçlarını kaybeder.
error_profile.collision: Yalın işitsel algı dalıyla kolayca karışır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Sözü kavramanın yanında ona uyma sonucu açıkça bulunur.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Her konuşanı dinleme ve söyleneni kabul etme eğilimi ayrıca kapsanır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal dikkatle dinlenen sözün kabul edilmesine uzanabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal anlama ile başlayıp uyma sonucuna varır; komşu dal dinleme, sessizce kulak verme ve kabul etme tutumunu daha geniş biçimde kapsar.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Sözün anlamı kavranır ve kabul ya da uyma gerçekleşebilir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Anlama gerçekleşmeden de ses kulakla algılanabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal, sözün kulağa ulaşmasından sonraki iletişim sürecinde art arda yer alır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu dal işitsel algıda tamamlanabilir; bu dal için sözün bilişsel olarak kavranması ve kimi bağlamlarda davranışa yön vermesi gerekir.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar karşılaştırıldı; kabul ederek dinleme ve yalın işitme, bu dalın sınırını en doğrudan açıklayan komşulardır.
branches.what_is_ar: السمع بمعنى فهم القول أو قبوله والعمل بموجبه والطاعة بعد الفهم
branches.source_phrase_ar: تارة عن الفهم وتارة عن الطاعة (mufradat)؛ فهمنا وارتسمنا (mufradat)؛ فهمنا وهم لا يفهمون (mufradat)؛ لم يستعملوا هذه الحواس استعمالا يجدي عليهم (tahdhib)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak sözü güzel ünü, bir haberin insanlar arasında yayılmasını, birini tanınır kılmayı ve başkaları duysun diye gösteriş yapmayı aynı dalda toplar. Dal kullanılabilir, ancak ün sonucu ile yayma eylemi ve gösteriş amacı tek bir eşanlamlı çekirdek gibi sunulmamalıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın ün ve yaygın söz edilme anlamı, bir şeyi yayma eyleminden ve insanların duyması amacıyla yapılan gösterişi bildiren söz öbeklerinden ayrı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişi veya şey hakkında sözün insanlar arasında yayılmasıyla tanınmışlık ya da ün oluşmasıdır. Bazı biçimler haberi yayma, birini övgüyle anılır kılma veya yapılan işi başkaları duysun diye sergileme eylemini anlatır.

facets.statement: Bir kişi veya şey hakkında söz geniş bir çevrede dolaşır ve tanınmışlık doğurur.
Ün, özellikle güzel ad ve olumlu anılma olarak gerçekleşebilir.
Ettirgen kullanımda bir haber yayılır veya bir kişinin adı öne çıkarılır.
Bir iş, insanlar duysun ve yapan tanınsın diye gösteriş amacıyla yapılabilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu kanıt, insanlar arasında yayılan sözden doğan ünü; haberi yayma, birini anılır kılma ve başkaları duysun diye gösteriş yapma kullanımlarıyla birlikte verir.

concept_gloss.applicability: İnsanlar arasında söz edilme yoluyla tanınmışlık veya ün oluşmasını en kısa doğal biçimde karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Sözün yayılması ile tanınmışlık sonucu arasındaki bağı korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kişinin adının insanlar arasında özellikle olumlu biçimde yayılması bağlamında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Yaygın tanınma ve güzel ad kazanma yönünü korur.
error_profile.loses: Olumsuz yayılmayı, haberi yayma eylemini ve gösteriş amacını dışarıda bırakır.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir haberin veya kişinin adının konuşularak geniş çevreye taşındığı ettirgen bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Sözü insanlar arasında yayma eylemini korur.
error_profile.loses: Yayılmanın doğurduğu ünü ve gösteriş amacıyla yapılan işi tek başına vermez.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir işin iç değerinden çok başkalarının onu duyması ve yapanı tanıması için gerçekleştirildiği bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Başkalarının duymasını amaçlayan gösteriş yönünü korur.
error_profile.loses: Genel ün ve haber yayma kullanımlarını kapsamaz.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: yaymak, tanınır kılmak veya adını öne çıkarmak

error_profile.preserves: Bilginin bir kişiye ulaştığı ilk aşamayı korur.
error_profile.loses: Sözün topluluk içinde yayılması ve ün doğurması sonucunu kaybeder.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Ün, güzel ad, haberi yayma ve duyulsun diye gösteriş yapma kullanımları birlikte bulunur.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Bir durumun açık ve görünür hâle gelmesi, kişilerce anılma olmadan da kapsanır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal bir şeyin insanlar arasında bilinir ve tanınır duruma gelmesini kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal söz edilme ve duyulma yoluyla ün oluşmasına odaklanır; komşu dal görünürlük ve açıklığı da kapsayan daha geniş bir tanınmışlık alanına sahiptir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Olumlu veya olumsuz yayılma, yayma eylemi ve gösteriş amacı da yer alabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Ün yalnızca iyi yöndeki ses ve tanınmışlıkla sınırlıdır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal kişinin insanlar arasında iyi adla tanınmasını kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu dal yalnız olumlu ünü anlatır; bu dal güzel adın yanında her tür yayılmayı, birini tanınır kılmayı ve duyulsun diye yapılan gösterişi de kapsar.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Yayılan sözün doğurduğu tanınmışlık ve gösteriş amacı önemlidir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Herhangi bir haberin açığa vurulup yayılması tek başına yeterlidir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Bir haberin insanlar arasında yayılması iki dalda da gerçekleşebilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal yayılmanın kişi veya şey hakkında ün ve söz edilme doğurmasına odaklanır; komşu dal ise bilginin açığa çıkarılıp dağıtılması eylemini anlatır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Adayların tümü değerlendirildi; genel tanınmışlık, yalnız iyi ün ve haber yayma dalları bu çok parçalı dalın temel sınırlarını gösterir.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه الاحتيال الخفي والخداع والكيد وصرف الغير عن قصده بحيلة، والمكر المحمود أو المذموم، وحيلة الحرب، والمكر المنسوب إلى الله بمعنى الجزاء.
يدخل فيه خدالة الساق وغلظها الحسن وامتلاؤها، وامرأة ممكورة الساقين، والمطوية الخلق من النساء.
